On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found 4 Release builds and 56 clang processes on 12 cores, all mine, in one worktree. Every ninja ran at its default -j (cores + 2), so 4 × 14 = 56. He pointed out that the orphaned processes were the smaller problem. The bigger one was that I put that many builds there at all.

What I did wrong, in order of weight:
1. I treated builds as free on a machine other sessions build on too. I never passed `-j`. I saw load 33, then 76, and started more builds anyway.
2. I restarted the build three times to change its target list or to slip in a small target. Each restart cost a full set of jobs. Waiting for the running build and adding targets afterwards cost nothing.
3. I went against the brief ("reuse the existing build; another session may be building") by configuring a fresh full-app build for an optional live check.
4. I blamed the slowness on "other sessions" without counting my own processes. That is the plausible-story-instead-of-checking failure from CLAUDE.md.
5. Mechanism: `pkill -f "cmake --build <dir>"` kills only the wrapper. Its `ninja -C <dir>` child keeps compiling as an orphan. I never checked that a stop had worked.

**Why:** the machine is shared. My extra jobs slow every other session, and two ninjas in one build dir can leave its records inconsistent.

**How to apply:**
- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. Cap jobs with `-- -j4` (fewer when load is above the core count).
- Decide the full target list once. Never restart a build to change it.
- Run one build per dir as its own process group (`set -m`, then kill with `kill -- -<pgid>`). After any stop, confirm with `pgrep -fl "ninja.*<dir>"`.
- Ask before a full-app build that the task did not require.

Related: [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

# Agent setup: one flow for every entry point

Written 2026-10-22, revised 2026-10-23 after the Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui (641c17f13e,
80ed1692ff). Status: DECIDED by Kenneth on 2026-10-23 (Decisions 1, 2, 3 and 5 chosen in the session that wrote this;
Decision 4's rule was proposed to him in the same message and not objected to; Decision 6 was settled by the
code). Untracked on purpose; never commit it. For a cold reader: section 3 is the design; section 2 is why.

## 1. The problem

The Agent (the React chat in the WebView pane) answers nothing until a provider is set up: an API key or a
connected AI tool. Several places in JusPrin need the Agent, and each answers "none is set up" its own way.
Calibration ("Calibrate…" on the printer chip, the filament slot and the Home printer card) would add one more.
Kenneth called the pattern clunky and surprising, and objected to the first calibration proposal: "On the
homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"

## 2. What the app does today (jusprin-newui at ea9f684de0, read 2026-10-23)

C. **The docked Agent pane's own entry** (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, `components/Setup.tsx`, `components/Panels.tsx`).

   docked pane's agent if any `jusprin_agent` setting changed (`open_preferences`, `reload_agent_config`).

### Decision 1 — Where the one setup flow lives

### Decision 3 — After setup completes, what happens?

1. **The surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent on the person's behalf (recommended).**
   `open_preferences` is modal and returns, so each caller only has to look again when it returns.
   - Print-issue bubble: "Ask AI" and "Resolve with AI" appear; the person picks one. (They had not chosen yet.)
   - Calibration: the Confirmation's primary action becomes "Start"; pressing it does what the handoff's 5.3 says.
   - Printer panel: the greeting continues, as today after in-panel setup.
   - Agent pane: the offer gives way to the composer, as today.
   Matches the onboarding delivery contract ("preserving project, plate, draft, choices, and pending task").
2. **Fire the action that was pressed** (send the issue question, start the test). Saves one press at the cost
   of remembering a request across a modal window and acting the moment a key passes.

Decision: Kenneth, 2026-10-23: option 1. The surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent on the person's behalf.

### Decision 4 — What cancel leaves behind

One rule: closing the window changes nothing underneath; the pending choice stays where it was.
- Print issue: the bubble still shows "Set up the agent…".
- Calibration: the Confirmation is still open with "Set up the agent…"; its Cancel closes it; no project is
  saved, closed or created.
- Printer panel: still open on its offer, with the form and "Open printer settings" available; never closed on
  the person's behalf.
- Agent pane: the offer or the thread with its bar, as before.

Decision: proposed to Kenneth 2026-10-23 as the one rule above and not objected to; recorded as decided.

### Decision 5 — Does the pane keep its own entry?

1. **Yes (recommended).** The offer, the setup bar and the chat list's "Connect an Agent" row stay; each opens
   Preferences › Agent, which is what the button already does once an agent exists.
2. **No.** Setup is reachable only from Preferences and from the actions that need it; an unconfigured pane
   would have no way to start.

Decision: Kenneth, 2026-10-23: option 1. The pane keeps its offer, its setup bar and the chat list row; each opens Preferences › Agent.

Settled by 641c17f13e: the Preferences window exists, so there is no interim sheet to build. Recorded here so a
cold reader does not look for one.

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)
Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.
The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.
This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.
## What success looks like
- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.
If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.
## Turn it on
Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.
`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:
```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```
JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.
Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.
**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.
Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.
The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.
## Drive state
Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.
```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |
No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:
```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```
`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.
Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.
## Print
Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.
If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.
On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).

### A system alert looked foreign next to OrcaSlicer's own questions

**Observed problem:** The "Previously opened file" question was a
`wxMessageDialog`, which on macOS is a system `NSAlert`: a narrow column with
the app icon above wrapped text and stacked buttons. Kenneth reviewed the
screenshots on 2026-10-14 and found it ugly next to every other question the

way (`ShellController::offer_agent_setup`, d0bce03db3). Other JusPrin
`wxMessageBox` and `wxMessageDialog` calls remain.

**Resolution:** The question uses OrcaSlicer's `MessageDialog` (`MsgDialog.hpp`),
with `SetButtonLabel` for its buttons. That dialog highlights Yes as the
primary button, so the suggested choice is put on Yes. Every `DPIAware`
dialog first passes through `answer_modal` (`DialogListeners.hpp`), and a
person's file open answers each one on its own. A dialog that asks the person
something during an open therefore needs a listener that returns
`kShowToPerson` for that one dialog.

Committed on `claude/reverent-northcutt-dd4d63` as **0994fd7b08**, one commit on top of jusprin-newui `ea9f684de0`. Every surface that needs the agent and finds none now has one button that opens Preferences › Agent. All tests pass except one check in the docked-pane harness run, which fails the same way on the unchanged code.

**Where each entry point goes now**
- **Print-issue bubble:** with no agent it draws one full-width primary button, "Set up the agent...", where Ask AI and Resolve with AI were. It calls `request_preferences("agent")` and the bubble stays open. The label ends in three dots, not "…": the canvas font has only basic and Latin‑1 characters, the same reason the existing "The assistant is replying..." note uses dots.
- **Docked Agent pane:** the "No agent connected" offer, the setup bar and the chat list's "Set up the agent" row all send `open_preferences` with section `agent`.
- **Printer panel:** its offer button does the same, and the panel stays open. When the window closes with changed agent settings, the shell also calls a new `PrinterPanel::reload_agent_config()`, so the greeting continues with the new agent. "Back" and "Browse the full printer list" are unchanged.
- **After the window closes:** with an agent, each surface carries on and nothing is sent for the person. Without one, nothing underneath changes.

**What was removed**
- `ShellController::offer_agent_setup` (the "Set up now / Not now" dialog) and `open_agent_setup`.
- `AgentHost::request_setup`, the `open_setup` message, `AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup` and `?embedded=1`.
- The printer panel's setup-completed listener and its `agent_configured` callback.
- On the page: `Setup.tsx` (the chooser, the key screen and the "Connected" banner) and the CSS only they used. `SetupLocalTool` and `AgentConnection.tsx` stay.

**A fix outside the brief:** the Vitest tests I moved to the Preferences page found a bug in the Preferences window. After connecting one AI tool failed, choosing another tool showed the old error under the new tool's name ("Cursor isn't installed"). The fix is one line in `SetupLocalTool.tsx`; the test failed before it and passes after.

**Tests**
- **Vitest:** 612 of 612 pass. New cases cover the offer, setup bar, chat-list row and printer panel each sending `open_preferences` with section `agent`, with no setup drawn, and the composer appearing once an agent is ready with nothing sent. They fail when the section is dropped. The key-row and AI-tool tests moved to the Preferences page.
- **Catch2:** `agent_bridge_tests` (409 cases) and `jusprin_tests` (132) pass.
- **Shell harness, `--print-issues`:** passes, 0 failures. The new steps check the single button, cancel, then a stored key bringing the two buttons back. The canvas captures match the board.
- **Shell harness, `--printer-setup`:** passes, 0 failures. When I took the printer panel reload out, two of its checks failed.
- **Shell harness, `--live-agent-unavailable`:** my new checks pass, but the existing `not_set_up_dock_is_one_live_offer` fails. It fails identically with the page built from the unchanged code: the fixture's edits make the chat non-empty, so the pane shows the setup bar instead of the full offer.
- **Builds:** run with `-j4` after checking load; none are still running.

**For the session that started me**
- That failing harness check needs its fixture or its expectation fixed; I left it alone.
- `SetupLocalTool`'s own tool-list step can no longer be reached, because Preferences always opens it on one tool. It could be removed.
- The run I killed while debugging may have left one harness data folder in the temp `jusprin-shell-*` folders. It never printed which one, so I deleted none of them.
